correctness.rationale: Exact elimination gives \(y=x\), \(z=x^2/c\), \(w=dx^3\), and the single condition \(x[(b-1)+(d-1/c)x^2]=0\). This yields the complete case split, including the singular locus \(dc=1\). At the source parameters \(R=-144\). Direct symbolic reconstruction of the origin Jacobian factors its characteristic polynomial by \((\lambda-1)\), so the universal linear instability is exact. The packaged rational checker was inspected but is only corroborative.
correctness.risk: The result concerns equilibria and local linearization only; it does not decide the existence or basin structure of the reported hyperchaotic attractor.

value.rationale: This is a complete correction of a published equilibrium geometry used in subsequent local-stability discussion. It identifies exactly when the advertised continuum actually exists and prevents applying a curve-based stability argument at parameters where no such curve is present.
value.risk: The correction does not by itself invalidate the source's numerical hyperchaos or encryption experiments.

final_claim: For the Ding--Ding four-dimensional flow \(\dot x=a(y-x),\ \dot y=bx-y-xz+w,\ \dot z=x^2-cz,\ \dot w=w-dx^3\) with \(a,b,c,d>0\), if \(dc\ne1\) and \(R=c(1-b)/(dc-1)\), the real equilibria are only the origin when \(R\le0\) and the origin plus \((\pm\sqrt R,\pm\sqrt R,R/c,\pm dR^{3/2})\) when \(R>0\); if \(dc=1\), a full equilibrium curve exists exactly when \(b=1\). At \((24,25,3,1/2)\), only the origin is an equilibrium, and the origin always has eigenvalue \(1\).
limitations: No claim about Lyapunov exponents, attractor existence, or cryptographic performance is made.
